title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day From Earth
paragraphs: On 18 November 2026, at 2:16 a.m. Pacific time, NASA's Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to be one light-day away from Earth – roughly 25.9 billion kilometres, or the distance light covers in 24 hours. Launched in 1977, the probe is moving at about 61,000 kilometres per hour, and a radio signal sent from it needs about a day to arrive.

Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012, and its twin, Voyager 2, followed in 2018. Both still measure changes in the Sun's magnetic field, but their plutonium-powered generators lose about four watts of power every year. To save energy, engineers switched off three devices on Voyager 1 and replaced them with lower-power alternatives, which should keep the current instruments running until at least the probes' 50th launch anniversaries next summer.

The milestone comes with a caveat. NASA has received no science or engineering data from Voyager 1 since 14 November, and engineers are analysing the cause. They could confirm the distance only because the spacecraft kept transmitting a carrier signal, which they combined with trajectory calculations. Project manager Suzanne Dodd said the probe will become "humanity's silent ambassador to the stars".

questions.a: They used the carrier signal together with trajectory calculations.
